title: Mexico at the UN: Velasco Defends Sovereignty and Calls for Renewing the Organization; Reiterates Support for Cuba and Recognition of Palestine
author: Arturo Sánchez Jiménez
content:
_This article by[Arturo Sánchez
Jiménez](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Arturo%20S%C3%A1nchez%20Jim%C3%A9nez)
originally appeared in the [September 25, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/25/politica/mexico-ante-
la-onu-velasco-defiende-soberania-y-llama-a-renovar-el-organismo), Mexico's
premier left wing daily newspaper._

Mexico “has shown that a country can cooperate closely and respectfully with
its partners and at the same time fully assert its sovereignty,” Foreign
Minister Roberto Velasco Álvarez said this Friday before the 81st General
Assembly of the United Nations (UN) in New York, where he maintained that the
organization faces “a challenge of enormous magnitude” to renew itself and
fulfill its founding mandate, in addition to reiterating **recognition of the
State of Palestine** and **support for Cuba** in the face of “any unilateral
economic measure” contrary to the UN Charter.

Representing President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, the foreign minister said that
this challenge of renewal implies “preserving humanity from the scourge of
armed conflicts, protecting human rights, improving the situation of millions
of vulnerable people, and ensuring the validity of international law.” He
added that the reform must also reach the organization’s leadership, in
reference to the upcoming election of the Secretary-General: “**in the United
Nations, too, it is time for women** ,” he stated.

Velasco Álvarez noted that Mexico, together with Norway, is promoting the UN80
Global group, aimed at a “more effective and more transparent” reform of the
organization, and maintained that the legitimacy of international institutions
depends on their capacity to “transform people’s lives in practice.”

He further explained that, together with Qatar, Norway, and Switzerland, the
country is promoting the strengthening of the organization’s mediation
capacities, under the premise that “every conflict that diplomacy prevents is
worth more than all those that force claims to resolve.”

The foreign minister insisted that the sovereignty of states does not depend
on their power.

> Sovereignty is not measured in armies or in material resources. All nations,
> all peoples, are worth the same before the law.
>
> Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco Álvarez

Mexico, he said, has shown that it is possible to “cooperate closely and
respectfully” with its partners “and at the same time fully assert its
sovereignty,” since “no nation builds its future from isolation” and “its
sovereignty is strengthened in dialogue and respectful collaboration with all
peoples.”

In his address, the Mexican official reiterated the country’s historic
position regarding Cuba. “We will continue sending humanitarian aid to meet
the most urgent needs of its population,” he said, and ratified “the
solidarity with the people of Cuba” that Mexico has maintained “for more than
six decades,” as well as the rejection “of any unilateral economic measure
contrary to the Charter of the United Nations.”

On the Middle East, Velasco Álvarez noted that Mexico “has defended the two-
state solution for decades” and recognizes the State of Palestine, “with the
right of its people to live in peace within secure and recognized borders.” He
maintained that, in the face of ongoing international conflicts,
“international law must prevail over force” and that “the civilian population
must be protected.”

The foreign minister framed these positions within the constitutional
principles of Mexican foreign policy—self-determination of peoples, non-
intervention, peaceful settlement of disputes, and the legal equality of
states—which, he said, coincide with the purposes of the San Francisco
Charter.

“**Mexico does not need to adapt its foreign policy to the Charter of the
United Nations, since it has it written into its Constitution** ,” he
expressed.

In his speech, Velasco reviewed what he called “five facts” of the Sheinbaum
government: the reduction of poverty by more than 13 million people between
2018 and 2024, the drop of around 51 percent in intentional homicides in 22
months, the **real increase of 154 percent in the minimum wage since 2018** ,
gender parity in the cabinet and Congress, and the exercise of a foreign
policy that he described as “sovereign and independent.”
